findings.title: A symlink in a tracked path parent preserves clean evidence and old review authority
findings.diagnosis: worktreeMatches Lstat/ReadFile the full leaf path. These operations follow symlinks in earlier components. A committed ignore rule can suppress enumeration of the replacement parent symlink. With equal target bytes and leaf mode, changedPaths is empty (or unchanged when another dirty file exists). CI appends revision-labelled evidence before or after the substitution. The full CLI advances Implementation review to Verification using an earlier review, with optional approval worktree binding absent and present.

evidence.observation: The leaf comparison never checks that each tracked path parent is a real directory.
Git reports D dir/tracked; pre/post HMA State values are equal and Worktree stays empty.
Both old-review paths append sequence 3 Verification records with machine_advanced=false; the human approval is valid for the current computed binding but the review artifact is stale in reality.
Pre-existing and command-induced substitution both append clean CI evidence with an empty WorktreeDigest.

fix.action: Before reading a tracked leaf, Lstat every relative parent component from the canonical repository root. Refuse a symlink or non-directory parent. Apply the same rule when hashing changed paths, including staged-only paths. Retire existing incomplete clean review identities and dirty worktree identities with new observation/review schema domains; require a fresh independent review.
fix.why: Git trees require directories for these parent components. Checking only the final leaf silently substitutes a different structure. Schema expiry prevents an old observation of the unsupported structure from authorizing the restored structure.

verification.method: Run TestAuditorR5TrackedDirectoryType, both TestAuditorR5CIDirectoryType cases, and FullArtifactMatrix parent-symlink with optional binding false/true.
verification.expected: Snapshot refuses explicitly or identifies the changed structure. CI and old-review progression append no records and preserve store bytes.

verification.method: Review a symlink-parent observation using current v2/v7 identities, restore a real directory with equal bytes, then replay that stored review after the fix.
verification.expected: Old incomplete identities refuse. A fresh review of a supported real-directory checkout succeeds.

verification.method: Retain clean/dirty, root-symlink, relative-root, linked-worktree, tracked leaf-symlink, committed-ignore and ordinary staged controls.
verification.expected: Supported unchanged cases succeed. Root aliases remain supported; a root alias is distinct from a symlink replacing a tracked internal directory.

fix.tradeoffs: Failing closed can reject unusual worktrees that replace tracked directories with links. Normal top-level aliases and tracked leaf symlinks must retain their current behavior. Schema expiry requires fresh captures/reviews.
fix.alternative: Represent every relevant parent component and link target in the artifact identity, including ignore-resistant enumeration. This is larger and risks admitting content outside the Git tree; explicit refusal is smaller.

findings.title: M3 final and disputed validation closure subcheck is not demonstrated
findings.disposition: BLOCK for full M3 closure; not an observed final-validation bypass
findings.diagnosis: The allowed Gate A M3 closure criterion explicitly requests final and disputed coverage. Supplied tests and independent probes demonstrate high/critical risk-rule and capability conjunction behavior. No final/disputed validation purpose is represented in RouteCoherenceRequest or tested as a host-derived context. This audit cannot treat those two purpose-specific checks as passed. This is an evidence/scope gap, not proof that final validation is currently accepted unsafely.

evidence.observation: The criterion ends: Cover final and disputed validation.
The request has Risk, but no final/disputed purpose. The kernel separation floor applies to high/critical risk.
All six independently constructed high/critical conjunction fixtures pass; they do not establish purpose-to-risk translation.

fix.action: Provide the supported trusted-host entry points and deterministic mapping for final/disputed validation, then add independent fixtures that exercise those contexts with weak rule IDs and same-family routes. If those entry points remain deferred, obtain an explicit human scope decision for this M3 subcheck and keep its absence visible.
fix.why: The audit must distinguish the repaired rule-selection defect from the remaining literal closure requirement. A label on a high-risk unit test does not test purpose-derived risk.

verification.method: Exercise final and disputed contexts through their supported host/API boundary with every applicable lower-risk rule, plus a valid separated control.
verification.expected: Same-family routes refuse regardless of selected rule. Valid independent routes remain eligible. If the surface is unsupported, it refuses explicitly and the scope decision records that limitation.

fix.tradeoffs: The minimum may be an evidence fixture and an explicit scope decision. Adding a new product context requires approved contract/binding design; do not widen permissions to create the test.
fix.alternative: Explicitly defer only the purpose-specific subcheck by human decision while retaining all repaired high/critical kernel constraints. No such decision was present in the allowed inputs.

limitations: Context isolation is fresh and blinded to prior closure reviews and implementer discussions. Required original defect-source documents contain historical assessments; they were used only as authoritative requirements. Source comments and supplied tests were inspected as artifacts.

Read-only source access was procedural, not an OS-enforced read-only mount. All test, probe and fault-injection changes are under this audit output directory. No files under /home/yeli/repos were edited; final freeze verification is reported separately.

The test target is a copied dirty worktree on main at HEAD 67965541b7032a585a68e48f3d10f4a998d5399e. .serena and the two architecture-amendment drafts were excluded from inspection and the copy. Their untracked hashes are retained only as requested freeze metadata.

The initial copy-under-/tmp suite exposed a harness test assumption. A second attempt used mismatched TMPDIR/GOTMPDIR. Both failed logs are retained. Final supplied-suite/race/harness runs align both variables and pass. These setup failures are not counted as product safety defects.

The storage model discards all unsynchronized directory entries at each checkpoint. It covers first/successor append and recovery of each crash image, not real hardware power loss or every possible subset/order of persisted entries. It assumes successfully file-synced immutable data persists. Source ordering and an intentionally broken negative control support the model.

Earlier named 40/55-checkpoint and r6/r7 reproduction scripts were not loaded before Phase 1. Independent equivalents were constructed. Exact historical binary replay was not performed; predecessor schema/digest expiry also has static domain-separation evidence. Case-insensitive-host execution was unavailable on this Linux case-sensitive filesystem.

Concurrency probes cover finite schedules. All five supported terminal outcomes have serial coverage in supplied tests; independent valid core API ordering uses ABORTED and Planning rewind. They do not exhaust every outcome, every unit rewind, every operation, and every timing combination.

Plan-derived dependency precision F05/C04/R3-03 is deferred to Gate D by the supplied human scope note. These rows remain PARTIAL and are not Gate B blockers. Conservative all-units invalidation is mandatory and was checked.
Jev is unavailable in the host tool inventory. Auditor judgment was used. No nested agents, model APIs, worker CLIs or external communications were used.

Passing synthetic telemetry, unit tests and this audit cannot grant stage approval, prove full host MVP conformance, or authorize release. The same-UID adversary is outside the supplied trusted-host threat model.
